title: Rust: Immutable Collections
description: Implement immutable/persistent data structures with structural sharing.

steps.title: Immutable List (Cons)
steps.description: Create an immutable linked list using `Rc` (reference counting). Define `enum ImList<T> { Cons(T, Rc<ImList<T>>), Nil }`. Create [1, 2, 3] and print.

verification.failureMessage: Create and print an immutable list [1,2,3].

steps.title: Structural Sharing
steps.description: Demonstrate structural sharing: create an immutable list `list1 = [1, 2, 3, 4]`. Create `list2` by prepending 0 to `list1`. Print both and show they share the tail.
hints: Both lists share the [1,2,3,4] tail (Rc handles reference counting).

verification.failureMessage: Create list1, create list2 by prepending, print both.

steps.title: Immutable Map (HAMT)
steps.description: Implement a simple persistent hash array mapped trie (HAMT) or a simpler persistent map using a sorted `Vec<(K, V)>` with structural sharing. Support `insert`, `get`, and `remove`.
hints: Simpler approach: persistent map using sorted Vec with structural sharing.
`insert` returns a new map with the entry added (doesn't modify old).
`get` does binary search on the sorted Vec.

verification.failureMessage: Create map, insert a key, and retrieve it.

steps.title: Immutability with Cloning
steps.description: Create a `Person` struct and demonstrate that after "modification" (using functional update), the original remains unchanged. Show both old and new versions.
hints: Bob has a different name but same age as Alice.

verification.failureMessage: Show original unchanged and new version with updates.

steps.title: Functional Operations
steps.description: Implement `map`, `filter`, and `fold` on `ImList<T>` that return new lists (not modifying the original). Chain: filter even numbers, map to squares, fold to sum. Test with [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
hints: `fn map<U, F>(&self, f: F) -> ImList<U> where F: Fn(&T) -> U`
Build the result by prepending in reverse order.
Chain: `list.filter(|x| x % 2 == 0).map(|x| x * x).fold(0, |a, x| a + x)` → 4+16=20

verification.failureMessage: Filter even, map to square, fold sum of [1..5] = 20.
